title: Consider the following statements regarding oral pathology diagnostic adjuncts. I. Use of these techniques eliminates the need for performing conventional biopsies. II. final: I &IV.

title: All of the following characteristics of a pathologic lesion raise suspicions for malignancy, EXCEPT:
final: Lesion feels attached to adjacent structures.
column5: Lesion and surrounding tissues are firm to touch.

title: Which of the following characteristics of an oral lesion should NOT be considered an indication for biopsy?
Oral & Maxillofacial Surgery Final Exam: Intrabony lesions that appear to be enlarging.
omfs: Visible or palpable submucosal swelling beneath clinically normal mucosa.
final: Any unknown lesion in a high-risk area for malignancy.
column5: Any lesion that does not resolve following routine clinical management (i.e. removal of local irritant) within 2 days
column6: Any lesion that is of extreme concern to the patient.

title: Which of the following statements regarding biopsy procedures is FALSE?

omfs: A patient who does not return for follow-up as recommended regarding a pathologic lesion should be contacted by various methods including phone and writing.
final: A biopsy log which includes patient identification, date of biopsy, information regarding how and when specimen was sent out and results returned, and communication with patient regarding these results should be maintained.
column5: As long as a histopathologic diagnosis obtained after biopsy of a suspicious lesion is benign, no further treatment or follow-up needs to be performed.
column6: Appropriate referral must be made after histopathologic diagnosis is obtained from a biopsy specimen.

title: Which of these statements is/are TRUE regarding INCISIONAL biopsies? I. This technique is generally utilized for lesions <1 cm. II. This technique is generally utilized for lesions >1 cm. III. This technique may be preferred for lesions that are in close proximity to vital structures. IV. If the pathologic diagnosis is benign, this technique will generally end up being the definitive surgical treatment.
final: I &IV.

title: Which of the following statements regarding the management of jaw tumors is TRUE?

omfs: Treatment decision making regarding surgical procedure may vary based on if the lesion remains intraosseous or has extended extraosseously.
final: Treatment decision making regarding surgical procedures may vary depending on whether or not reconstruction is anticipated.

title: Consider the following jaw lesions and treatments: Lesions:      I. Odontoma, Cementoblastoma, Aneurysmal bone cyst II. Ameloblastoma, Myxoma III. title: Which of the following statements regarding jaw tumors is TRUE?

column5: Frozen sections may be obtained to help determine if an adequate amount of tissue has been excised.

title: Which of the following statements is FALSE?

title: Which of the following statements regarding a periapical abscess is FALSE?

title: Hemorrhage after dental procedures can be prevented by or treated by:

title: You are extracting a lower right third molar with pericoronitis that is in close proximity to the inferior alveolar nerve. You have almost completely delivered the tooth from the socket, but a piece of the distal root has fractured off. What do you do?

title: You have extracted a lower left third molar on a 21 year-old male. The socket won't stop bleeding after you have applied pressure for ten minutes. title: An 8-year-old presents with a pulp exposure due to a traumatic crown fracture on a permanent central incisor. You determine the pulpal and periapical diagnosis to be healthy. The root is not completely formed. The best procedure here is:

omfs: Always perform root canal therapy up to the fracture line.
